jobs.title: Carrot: Director, Information Security
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote

About Carrot:

Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each member’s life. More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries – from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between. Carrot's comprehensive clinical program delivers industry-leading cost savings for plan sponsors and award-winning experiences and improved outcomes for millions of people worldwide.

Carrot is widely regarded as a defining force in healthcare innovation as a recipient of several top-tier awards, including Fast Company's 'Most Innovative Companies' and CNBC's '100 Barrier Breaking Startups'. The company is regularly cited by leading global outlets — including The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, NPR, ABC News, and Harvard Business Review — as a leading voice on digital health, the future of work, and family health. Learn more at get-carrot.com.

The Opportunity 

Carrot is looking for a Director, Information Security to lead the security program that protects the highly sensitive fertility and family-building data of members around the world. You will set the security strategy, own both corporate security (GRC, incident response, security awareness, vendor risk) and product security (application, cloud and infrastructure security, secure development lifecycle), and serve as the trusted voice on Carrot's security posture with executives, auditors, and enterprise customers.

Day to day, you will balance setting direction with staying close to the work: prioritizing risk with Engineering and IT, guiding audit and certification cycles, coaching a small and talented team, and joining customer conversations where security is part of the buying decision. Carrot has already earned SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, HITRUST, and PCI DSS compliance, so this role is about taking a strong foundation to the next level of maturity, not starting from scratch.

What makes this role different is the combination of stakes and influence. Few security leaders get to protect data this personal, at global scale, while working directly with executive leadership and shaping how a health platform is built, sold, and trusted.

What You’ll Own

In this role, you will:

  • Lead Carrot's security strategy and roadmap, using a recognized maturity model (such as C2M2 or NIST CSF) to prioritize investments and report progress to executive leadership
  • Own the full security program across corporate security (GRC, incident management, security awareness, third-party risk) and product security (application security, cloud and infrastructure security, secure SDLC)
  • Partner with Engineering, especially the Internal Platform team, to build security into how Carrot designs, ships, and operates its systems, going beyond compliance
  • Lead internal risk assessments across application, cloud, and corporate environments and turn the results into prioritized technical safeguards
  • Own the compliance portfolio, including SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST, PCI DSS, and HIPAA, and prepare Carrot for additional frameworks such as ISO 27001 as the business requires
  • Direct incident response readiness, including playbooks, tabletop exercises, executive communication, and post-incident learning
  • Represent Carrot's security posture to employers, health plans, and health systems through security reviews, questionnaires, and strategic sales conversations
  • Work with Legal and Privacy to meet global data protection requirements (HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA/CPRA) for member health data
  • Build, coach, and grow the security team, balancing hands-on execution with delegation as the team scales
  • Manage the security budget, tooling, and vendor relationships, and tailor security guidance for a remote-first workforce and physical offices

What Success Looks Like  

In your first 12–18 months, you will have:

  • A documented, executive-endorsed security strategy and multi-year roadmap with clear priorities, owners, and measures of progress
  • Clean outcomes on recurring audits and certifications (SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST, PCI DSS), with remediation items closed on schedule
  • A tested incident response program, with regular tabletop exercises completed and lessons learned built back into the program
  • A measurable reduction in high-risk vulnerabilities and open security findings, with remediation timelines agreed on with Engineering
  • A living risk register and vendor security review process that leaders rely on to make decisions
  • A security team with defined roles, clear growth paths, and the right capacity for Carrot's growth, including key hires made
  • Faster, more consistent security reviews for Sales and Customer Success, with fewer escalations from enterprise customers
  • A clear plan, and visible progress, on any additional frameworks the business prioritizes, such as ISO 27001

About You

You likely have:

  • A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field (or equivalent experience)
  • 10+ years of experience in technology, including 5+ years in information security and at least 3 years leading security teams
  • A security certification such as CISSP or CISM
  • Experience leading the security function at a late-stage startup, scale-up, or public company
  • Working depth in healthcare data protection and privacy frameworks, including HIPAA, GDPR, and CCPA/CPRA
  • Experience overseeing enterprise frameworks and audits such as SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST, PCI DSS, and ISO 27001
  • Strong knowledge of application, network, and cloud security (AWS and Azure) and frameworks such as NIST CSF and OWASP
  • Experience running core security programs, including incident response, risk management, vulnerability management, penetration testing, and security awareness
  • Executive-level communication skills and confidence engaging customers and sales teams on security requirements
  • Experience managing budget and allocating resources across people, tools, and vendors

 

Nice to Have ⭐

While not required, we would be especially excited if you bring:

  • Experience leading security through a major company event such as an IPO, acquisition, or large-scale audit cycle
  • A background in healthcare, digital health, or another highly regulated, high-trust environment
  • Experience leading security in a remote-first, globally distributed company
  • Familiarity with compliance automation platforms such as Drata
  • Experience building a security engineering practice alongside platform and infrastructure teams

 

Why This Role Matters

Members trust Carrot with some of the most personal information a person can share, often during some of the most meaningful moments of their lives. Protecting that trust is not a back-office function. It is what allows employers, health plans, and health systems to bring Carrot to millions of people worldwide.

As Carrot grows, security leadership shapes how we build, how we sell, and how we show up for customers. In this role, you will make security a strength that members and customers can see and rely on, and build a team that keeps raising the bar as the business scales.

Why Candidates Join Carrot

Carrot offers the opportunity to do meaningful work in service of a deeply human mission.

Highlights include:

  • A mission-driven company focused on expanding access to fertility and family-forming care globally.
  • A high-growth environment where leaders are empowered to shape strategy and drive impact.
  • Competitive compensation, equity, and comprehensive benefits.
  • Flexible Time Off and a culture that actively encourages employees to recharge.
  • Comprehensive parental leave and family-forming benefits.
  • A collaborative, inclusive, and values-driven culture.
  • The opportunity to work alongside passionate, thoughtful teammates committed to improving healthcare outcomes worldwide.

 

Compensation: 

Carrot offers a holistic Total Rewards package designed to support our employees in all aspects of their lives inside and outside of work, including health and wellness benefits, retirement savings plans, short- and long-term incentives, parental leave, family-forming assistance, and a competitive compensation package. The starting base salary for this position will range from $188,000.00 - $245,000.00. Actual compensation may vary from posted base salary depending on your confirmed job-related skills and experience. 

 

Fraud and Security Notice: Please note that all communication regarding job opportunities at Carrot will come exclusively from an @get-carrot.com email address. If you receive messages from any other domain, please disregard them and report the incident to: securityreporting@get-carrot.com

 

A Note on AI

At Carrot, we believe AI can help us work smarter, move faster, and create more meaningful experiences for our members, customers, and each other. While not every role requires deep technical AI expertise, we value people who are curious, eager to learn, and excited to thoughtfully incorporate AI into their day-to-day work.

For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement—and we'll call that out clearly in the qualifications. For everyone else, we're looking for people who embrace new ways of working, use AI responsibly to improve quality and efficiency, and continue to learn as the technology evolves.

Why Carrot?

Carrot has received national and international recognition for its pioneering work, including Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies and World Changing Ideas, Inc. Power Partners, and Modern Healthcare’s Innovators. Carrot’s global workforce has been acknowledged with several accolades, including Fortune’s Best Workplaces in Healthcare, Great Place to Work, and Age-Friendly Employer certifications. Carrot is regularly featured in media reporting on issues related to the future of work, women in leadership, and healthcare innovation, including MSNBC, The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, CNBC, National Public Radio, Harvard Business Review, and more. Learn more at carrotfertility.com.

  • Proactively engages with senior-level and strategically important customer/prospect representatives, influencing product-related decisions.
  • Develops executive-level credibility and trust, influencing customer-focused solution development and purchasing decisions.
  • Build independent relationships to identify growth opportunities.
  • Act as a go-to subject matter expert for specific product areas, industries, or complex technical domains.

Adoption and Expansion

  • Architect highly customized and integrated solutions for identified Agency use cases
  • Collaborate with Solution Architects in providing guidance on solution design for new use cases.
  • Support customer identification of value and ROI. Support customer use case library aligned to data strategy and business value, leveraging the services team when and where required.
  • Actively support account growth strategies with the AE/AM.
  • Understand in detail the specific differentiators for Collibra solutions, including strengths and weaknesses of competition.
  • Provide thought leadership on best practices for adoption and technical optimizations. 
  • Influences product and service direction to enhance overall client experience.
  • Design and validate future-state technical architectures for major transformation projects, integrating across vast complex ecosystems
  • Mapping solutions to value across large and dynamic customers, bridging both business and technical requirements.
  • Advising and supporting customers’ technical stakeholders to accelerate Collibra adoption and value realization, i.e., be the primary point of contact for technical and product-related queries. 
  • Architect solutions that function across complex Federal environments, including on-premises, hybrid cloud, and disconnected/classified networks.
  • Help agencies build a "Unified Data Language" to facilitate secure data sharing between departments while maintaining strict access controls and data labeling.

Customer Support

  • Address technical questions, mitigate risks, and overcome objections related to security, scalability, integration and implementation.
  • Identify adoption roadblocks and ensure successful product usage. 
  • Drive technical resolution and best practices for common challenges. 
  • Document customer use cases and adoption challenges, providing guidance on adoption/value realization best practices.

Teaming

  • Provides onboarding assistance for CEs and allied sales team members.
  • Contributes to Customer Engineering participation in major projects and provides forward-looking technical guidance.
  • Maintain expert-level product knowledge across the portfolio.
  • Works internally to improve product marketing messaging and educate Sales/CEs.
  • Provides team members with technical and process guidance and advice.
  • Build and execute account specific competitive strategies, and contribute to the broader Collibra competitive landscape analysis. Understand the broader technology ecosystem and future trends.
  • Packages best practices and lessons learned into thought leadership, methodologies, and published assets to improve Customer Engineering processes.
  • Owns Customer Engineering participation in major projects and provides forward-looking technical guidance.
  • Supporting sales and marketing activities, webcasts, field enablement, and asset creation.
  • Providing advice and feedback to product management and engineering to enhance Collibra solutions and offerings.

You have

  • 5+ years in Sales Engineering or Technical Consulting, specifically supporting U.S. Federal Government customers with 4+ years working in the Data/SaaS space.
  • Proficiency in SQL and deep familiarity with Federal data stacks (e.g., Snowflake Government Data Cloud, AWS GovCloud, Azure Government, and Palantir) are a plus.
  • Working knowledge of NIST 800-53, FISMA, and the Federal Data Strategy.
  • Proven ability to navigate the Federal procurement cycle and build long-term relationships with Agency CDOs, CTOs, and Program Managers.
  • Experience should include a broad range of disciplines, including value-based selling, cost-benefit analysis, ROI analysis, process and project management.
  • Experience in regulatory compliance and or (financial/IT) audit is a plus. 
  • Experience working with leading PaaS providers, data lakes, databases, and integration platforms is required.
  • Familiarity in enterprise security solutions such as LDAP or Kerberos.
  • Experience working with Data Quality, Data Pipelines, Data Orchestration, and/or Job Control tools.
  • Knowledgeable of at least least two or three of the following: data management processes, including data governance, data stewardship, master data management, data cataloging, and business rules management
  • Experienced with Collibra or comparable technologies
  • Demonstrated proficiency in leveraging AI tools (e.g., Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, Copilot) to solve real-world business challenges, drive measurable outcomes, or streamline workflows.
  • A bachelor’s degree or equivalent related working experience is required. 
  • Hold active security clearance (Secret/TS).
  • Because this role supports the U.S. government business, it is required that you are a U.S. citizen who resides on U.S. soil.

You are

  • Exceptional in communication, presentation and interpersonal skills including the ability to communicate effectively and build relationships within government entities.
  • Fast learner with an aptitude for grasping complex technical concepts.
  • Excellent organization and stakeholder management skills.
  • A proven collaborator and liaison with all levels and departments within an organization, with experience and success in both partner and contractor-heavy environments.
  • Confident in dispensing knowledge to a highly skilled and experienced audience.
  • Able to demonstrate a thorough understanding of business needs and revenue potential for accounts in the region.

Measures of success

  • Within your first month, you will become familiar with Collibra Public Sector and understand our customer landscape.
  • Within your second month, you should confidently conduct discovery with customers and prospects, initial product demonstrations, and be able to present solutions aligned to customer value.
  • Within your third month, you will become a voice for Collibra within your accounts and for your accounts back within Collibra - educating external and internal stakeholders on features, roadmap, and new use cases. Additionally you will drive operational excellence by ensuring the sales process runs smoothly and efficiently.

Compensation for this role

The standard base salary range for this position is $140,000 - $175,000 per year. This position is eligible for additional commission-based compensation. Salary offers are based on a combination of factors, including, but not limited to, experience, skills, and location.

In addition to base salary, we offer a competitive total rewards package, including bonus potential, equity for eligible roles, a Flex Fund monthly stipend, pension/401k plans, and more.

Benefits at Collibra

Collibra recognizes and values that everyone has different needs, interests, and life goals. These flexible offerings sit on a foundation of competitive compensation, health coverage, and time off. Learn more about Collibra’s benefits.

With this, we proudly consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, pregnancy, sex, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information, physical or mental disability, HIV status, registered domestic partner status, caregiver status, marital status, veteran or military status, citizenship status or any other legally protected category. jobs.title: Carrot: Business Intelligence Analyst
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote

About Carrot:

Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each member’s life. More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries – from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between. Carrot's comprehensive clinical program delivers industry-leading cost savings for plan sponsors and award-winning experiences and improved outcomes for millions of people worldwide.

Carrot is widely regarded as a defining force in healthcare innovation as a recipient of several top-tier awards, including Fast Company's 'Most Innovative Companies' and CNBC's '100 Barrier Breaking Startups'. The company is regularly cited by leading global outlets — including The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, NPR, ABC News, and Harvard Business Review — as a leading voice on digital health, the future of work, and family health. Learn more at get-carrot.com.

The Opportunity

Carrot is seeking a Business Intelligence Analyst to join our BI function as it scales to meet, and anticipate, the needs of the organization and its clients. This is an executional role providing essential analytics support across the company: you will gather requirements, field ad hoc and recurring data requests, and build the reporting dashboards that leaders across Carrot rely on to make decisions.

You will work hands-on with modern data tooling, including SQL, dbt, and enterprise BI platforms, and partner with teams across the business to translate their questions into clear, trustworthy answers. The BI team is highly cross-functional and sits alongside Data Engineering, making this a strong opportunity to sharpen technical skills while building broad business context in a mission-driven environment.

 

What You’ll Own

In this role, you will:

  • Design and build data models in SQL with a focus on correctness, clarity, and reusability
  • Build and maintain dashboards and reports that track key business metrics and inform decision-making across the company
  • Conduct ad hoc analyses to answer high-priority business questions from stakeholders across the organization
  • Collaborate with teams across Carrot to understand their data domains, reporting needs, and success metrics
  • Contribute to data quality, documentation, and self-service BI capabilities as the function scales

 

What Success Looks Like  

In your first 12–18 months, you will have:

  • Delivered accurate, well-documented dashboards and reports that stakeholders across the company trust and use regularly
  • Fully ramped on Carrot's data stack and core data domains, independently owning recurring and ad hoc reporting requests
  • Built strong working relationships with cross-functional partners and established yourself as a reliable analytics resource
  • Improved turnaround and consistency of reporting by creating reusable data models and reducing manual work

 

About You 

You likely have:

  • A Bachelor's Degree
  • Intermediate-to-advanced SQL experience: ability to write advanced queries using joins, common table expressions, and window/analytic functions
  • Experience with data visualization software (e.g., Tableau, Looker, DOMO, or Power BI) to bring data insights to life for broad audiences
  • Basic statistics proficiency: experiment design, hypothesis testing, statistical significance, probability, and distributions
  • Ability to translate business intelligence needs from a variety of stakeholders into technical execution and clear presentation
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical information to non-technical audiences

 

Nice to Have ⭐

While not required, we would be especially excited if you bring:

  • Experience using dbt to transform, test, and document data
  • Experience working with healthcare industry data or in other complex, regulated data environments
  • Experience in a high-growth environment
  • Familiarity with version control systems (Git preferred)
  • Understanding of effective data modeling strategies and implementations

 

Why This Role Matters

Data is central to how Carrot operates and grows. Leaders across the company depend on accurate, timely reporting to serve members, support customers, and make sound business decisions. As a Business Intelligence Analyst, you will be the connective tissue between raw data and those decisions, ensuring the organization runs on insights it can trust.

Your work directly supports Carrot's mission of expanding access to fertility and family-building care worldwide. Better data means better decisions for the members and customers who rely on Carrot every day.

 

Interview Process 

We believe in a thoughtful and transparent interview process designed to create alignment for both candidates and our team.

For this role, candidates can expect:

  1. Recruiter Screen — 30 minutes
  2. Hiring Manager Interview — 45 minutes
  3. Cross-Functional Panel Interviews — 45 minutes
  4. Performance Task — 60 minutes

Throughout the process, we will share additional context about the team, business priorities, customer landscape, and what success looks like in this role.

 

Why Candidates Join Carrot

Carrot offers the opportunity to do meaningful work in service of a deeply human mission.

Highlights include:

  • A mission-driven company focused on expanding access to fertility and family-forming care globally.
  • A high-growth environment where leaders are empowered to shape strategy and drive impact.
  • Competitive compensation, equity, and comprehensive benefits.
  • Flexible Time Off and a culture that actively encourages employees to recharge.
  • Comprehensive parental leave and family-forming benefits.
  • A collaborative, inclusive, and values-driven culture.
  • The opportunity to work alongside passionate, thoughtful teammates committed to improving healthcare outcomes worldwide.

 

Compensation

Carrot offers a holistic Total Rewards package designed to support our employees in all aspects of their life inside and outside of work, including health and wellness benefits, retirement savings plans, short- and long-term incentives, parental leave, family-forming assistance, and a competitive compensation package. The starting base salary for this position will range from $98,000.00- $125,000.00. Actual compensation may vary from posted base salary depending on your confirmed job-related skills and experience. 

 

Fraud and Security Notice: Please note that all communication regarding job opportunities at Carrot will come exclusively from an @get-carrot.com email address. If you receive messages from any other domain, please disregard them and report the incident to: securityreporting@get-carrot.com

 

A Note on AI

At Carrot, we believe AI can help us work smarter, move faster, and create more meaningful experiences for our members, customers, and each other. While not every role requires deep technical AI expertise, we value people who are curious, eager to learn, and excited to thoughtfully incorporate AI into their day-to-day work.

For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement—and we'll call that out clearly in the qualifications. For everyone else, we're looking for people who embrace new ways of working, use AI responsibly to improve quality and efficiency, and continue to learn as the technology evolves.

Why Carrot?

Carrot has received national and international recognition for its pioneering work, including Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies and World Changing Ideas, Inc. Power Partners, and Modern Healthcare’s Innovators. Carrot’s global workforce has been acknowledged with several accolades, including Fortune’s Best Workplaces in Healthcare, Great Place to Work, and Age-Friendly Employer certifications. Carrot is regularly featured in media reporting on issues related to the future of work, women in leadership, and healthcare innovation, including MSNBC, The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, CNBC, National Public Radio, Harvard Business Review, and more. Learn more at carrotfertility.com. 

 

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/carrot-business-intelligence-analyst

jobs.title: Fastly: Threat Detection Analyst (Japanese Speaking desirable)
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Australia (Remote)

Fastly helps people stay better connected with the things they love. Fastly’s edge cloud platform enables customers to create great digital experiences quickly, securely, and reliably by processing, serving, and securing our customers’ applications as close to their end-users as possible — at the edge of the Internet. The platform is designed to take advantage of the modern internet, to be programmable, and to support agile software development. Fastly’s customers include many of the world’s most prominent companies, including GitHub, Yelp, Paramount, and JetBlue.

We're building a more trustworthy Internet. Come join us.

Threat Detection Analyst - (Japanese speaking desirable)

Fastly is seeking a Threat Detection Analyst to join our dedicated Customer Security Operations Centre. In this role, you will be a frontline defender for Fastly’s global enterprise customers. You will leverage our edge cloud platform and an array of security products in monitoring traffic, detect sophisticated anomalies, and deploy real-time mitigations against DDoS, Bot, and Web Application attacks.

This is a high-impact role where you act as a strategic partner for our Managed Security Service (MSS) clients, providing the expert visibility and rapid response necessary to address internet-scale threats.

What you’ll Do :

  • Active Incident Response: Lead the identification and mitigation of high-impact security events. You will analyze sophisticated traffic patterns and implement precise countermeasures, including rate limiting and custom WAF & Security rules to neutralize threats in real-time.
  • Managed Security Delivery: Serve as a primary security consultant for MSS Customers. This involves continuous tuning and refining of security policies to optimize detection accuracy and maintaining a hardened security posture tailored to each client's unique environment.
  • Advanced Threat Hunting: Conduct data-driven investigations using log analysis to uncover potential threats and hardenings opportunities
  • Security Intelligence & Reporting: Author comprehensive After Action Reports (AARs) and monthly security summaries. You will translate complex telemetry and attack data into high-level actionable insights for customer stakeholders.
  • Strategic Communication: Act as the Subject Matter Expert (SME) during active security incidents. You will provide clear, calm, and professional guidance via real-time communication channels, ensuring customers are informed and confident in our defensive strategy.

What we are looking for :

  • Web Security Expertise: Comprehensive understanding of the OWASP Top 10 and advanced attack vectors (e.g., Credential Stuffing, API Abuse, and Layer 7 DDoS). You can interpret raw payloads to distinguish between malicious intent and legitimate traffic.
  • Protocol Proficiency: Deep technical knowledge of the internet stack, specifically HTTP/S, TCP/IP, DNS, and TLS. You should be comfortable analyzing handshake processes, header structures, and status codes.
  • Analytical Rigor: A methodical approach to digital forensics and incident response. You possess the ability to correlate disparate data points within JSON or CSV logs to reconstruct an attack narrative.
  • Communication Excellence: The ability to distill complex technical findings into concise, professional, and empathetic communications for both technical and non-technical audiences.

We’ll be super impressed if you have experience in any of these:

  • Proficiency in Python or Bash for log parsing and workflow automation.
  • Experience with Infrastructure as Code/Security as Code(SaC) (Terraform) or edge-based configurations.
  • Industry-standard certifications such as CompTIA CySA+, GCIH, or Security+.

Work Hours:

  • This position will require you to be available during core business hours.
  • Tuesday to Saturday : 10 am to 6 PM AEST and 11 am to 7 pm AEDT 

Work Location(s) & Travel Requirements

This position is a remote position based out of (locality), with the possibility of becoming a hybrid position as Fastly expands its presence in the region.

This position will require travel to the US and Internationally, as required by your role or requested by your manager.

Benefits:

We care about you. Fastly works hard to create a positive environment for our employees, and we think your life outside of work is important too. We support our teams with great benefits that start on the first day of your employment with Fastly. Curious about our offerings?

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to meet your needs. Our offerings may vary depending on the country where you work and are subject to change.

 

Why Fastly?

  • We have a huge impact. Fastly is a small company with a big reach. Not only do our customers have a tremendous user base, but we also support a growing number of open source projects and initiatives. Outside of code, employees are encouraged to share causes close to their heart with others so we can help lend a supportive hand.

  • We value diversity. Growing and maintaining our inclusive and diverse team matters to us. We are committed to being a company where our employees feel comfortable bringing their authentic selves to work and have the ability to be successful -- every day.

  • We are passionate. Fastly is chock full of passionate people and we’re not ‘one size fits all’. Fastly employs authors, pilots, skiers, parents (of humans and animals), makeup geeks, coffee connoisseurs, and more. We love employees for who they are and what they are passionate about.

We’re always looking for humble, sharp, and creative folks to join the Fastly team. If you think you might be a fit please apply! A fully completed application and resume or CV are required when applying.

All job applications must be submitted through our official careers site at www.fastly.com/about/careers. We will never request sensitive information, such as your Social Security number, bank account or credit card information during the application process. All official communication will come from an @fastly.com or @recruiting.fastly.com email address.

Fastly is committed to ensuring equal employment opportunity and to providing employees with a safe and welcoming work environment free of discrimination and harassment. Our employment decisions are based on business needs, job requirements and individual qualifications. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, national origin, family or parental status, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances.

Consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and federal or state disability laws, Fastly will provide reasonable accommodations for applicants and employees with disabilities. If reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please contact your Recruiter, or the Fastly Employee Relations team at candidateaccommodations@fastly.com or 501-287-4901. 

Fastly collects and processes personal data submitted by job applicants in accordance with our Privacy Policy. Please see our privacy notice for job applicants.

jobs.title: OpenBase LLC: Head of Growth & Operations
jobs.description:
Headquarters: US
URL: https://openbase.ai/

Head of Growth & Operations — Openbase.ai

Full-time | Remote | Reports directly to the Founder

About Openbase

Openbase.ai is an AI gateway that helps developers and businesses access multiple AI models through one API. We simplify model access, routing, and usage management so teams can focus on building AI products.

Our MVP is ready. We are hiring a hands-on leader to own our go-to-market strategy, day-to-day business execution, and journey from launch to our first 10,000 users.

The opportunity

You will work directly with the founder to turn Openbase into a growing business with repeatable customer acquisition, strong retention, and disciplined operations.

You will own the commercial execution: finding our first customers, testing acquisition channels, improving onboarding, building partnerships, and organizing the people and systems needed to grow.

Our ambition is 10,000 users. Your responsibility is to build a credible, measurable path toward that goal, with clear milestones for activated developers, retained customers, paying accounts, and profitable usage.

What you will own

1. Go-to-market and customer acquisition

  • Identify our strongest initial customer segments, including AI startups, independent developers, agencies, and software teams.
  • Develop our positioning and explain why developers should choose Openbase.
  • Launch and improve acquisition across X, SEO, visibility in AI search engines, developer communities, partnerships, and targeted outbound.
  • Test paid campaigns with clear budgets, conversion tracking, and criteria for scaling or stopping.
  • Build a growth roadmap with weekly experiments and monthly acquisition targets.

2. Developer activation and retention

  • Own the journey from website visit to signup, first successful API request, first payment, and ongoing usage.
  • Work with engineering to remove onboarding friction and improve documentation, quickstarts, and integration examples.
  • Speak directly with developers to understand why they try Openbase, keep using it, or leave.
  • Establish onboarding communications, customer support processes, and reactivation campaigns.
  • Turn successful customer implementations into case studies and referrals.

3. Sales and partnerships

  • Personally source and close early customers.
  • Build a qualified pipeline of startups and businesses with recurring AI usage.
  • Develop distribution partnerships with developer tools, AI communities, accelerators, and complementary platforms.
  • Coordinate technical evaluations and customer requirements with engineering.
  • Build a repeatable sales process as demand grows.

4. Business execution and team management

  • Translate company goals into weekly priorities, accountable owners, and delivery dates.
  • Recruit and manage freelancers, agencies, and future hires across growth, content, developer relations, and customer success.
  • Own marketing budget allocation and evaluate spending against business results.
  • Coordinate customer needs with product and engineering priorities.
  • Implement practical workflows and automation that reduce manual work.

5. Metrics and commercial performance

  • Maintain a dashboard covering acquisition, activation, retention, paying customers, and API usage.
  • Track customer acquisition cost, conversion rates, and retention by channel.
  • Separate customer spending from provider costs and Openbase’s retained revenue and gross profit.
  • Monitor promotional credits and infrastructure costs so growth remains economically sound.
  • Give the founder a clear weekly view of results, blockers, and decisions needed.

What we are looking for

  • Experience leading growth and commercial execution at an early-stage SaaS, API, developer-tools, or AI infrastructure company.
  • Evidence of acquiring users from an early starting point, with specific numbers and your personal contribution.
  • Understanding of developer audiences and how technical products earn adoption.
  • Ability to understand an API integration, follow documentation, and discuss onboarding issues with engineers.
  • Hands-on ability to run experiments, analyze funnels, conduct customer calls, and manage delivery.
  • Experience managing budgets and external specialists.
  • Strong written English, sound judgment, and comfort working directly with a founder.

Experience with usage-based pricing, developer relations, technical SEO, and AI model platforms is particularly relevant.

Why join

  • Direct ownership of Openbase’s launch and growth.
  • Close collaboration with the founder and engineering team.
  • The opportunity to build the commercial function from its earliest stage.
  • Scope to take on broader company leadership as the business grows.

How to apply

Send your CV or LinkedIn profile, together with brief answers to:

  1. Which product have you helped grow? Include starting users, ending users, timeframe, budget, and your exact role.
  2. Which acquisition channels produced retained or paying customers?
  3. How would you approach Openbase’s first 1,000 activated developers?
  4. What would you personally execute, and where would you use specialists?
  5. What are your location, availability, and compensation expectations?

Include an example of a growth experiment or operating system you built. Share only information you are authorized to disclose.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/openbase-llc-head-of-growth-operations

jobs.title: Airbnb: Senior Manager, Quality, Volume Tiers
jobs.description:
Headquarters: United States
URL: https://careers.airbnb.com/life-at-airbnb/

Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join:

The Senior Quality Lead, Volume Tiers is the single accountable leader for quality measurement, insights, and continuous improvement across Airbnb's highest-volume Community Support functions. This role owns the end-to-end quality program for:

  1. Global English (GE)
  2. Rest of World (ROW; which is comprised of 9 different languages)
  3. Elevated Support

GE and ROW span across multiple service tiers: Resolutions 1, 2, and 3, Dedicated Service Support (DSS), Dedicated Managed Host Support (DMHS); supported across a global partner network operating 24/7 in dozens of languages.

The Difference You will Make:

This is a senior leadership role operating at the intersection of strategy and execution. The Senior Quality Lead will break down silos within the Quality organization, establish a unified operating model, and leverage AI-powered tools to scale quality insights. This leader will work closely with Service Delivery, Training, Business Process Improvement, and other stakeholders to ensure alignment on priorities, remediate issues, and ensure Airbnb is providing its global partner network a unified set of priorities.

The successful candidate will establish themselves as a credible partner to stakeholders and be recognized internally as the voice of quality for the Volume Tier portfolio.

A Typical Day:

Strategic Leadership & Program Ownership

  • Own and execute the Volume Tier quality strategy aligned to several critical priorities: breaking silos, aligning with stakeholders, defining a clear operating model, and driving measurable impact.
  • Consolidate fragmented QA frameworks across GE and ROW into a unified operating model, eliminating inconsistent processes, divergent NPS detractor approaches, and incompatible quality signals.
  • Represent Volume Tier quality in WBRs, MBRs, QBRs, and cross-functional planning forums; bring a proactive, narrative-led perspective that gives leadership visibility before problems surface in operational reviews.

Measurement & Quality Execution

  • Oversee QA evaluation execution across all Volume Tier partner sites globally, ensuring consistent application of QA processes and frameworks.
  • Lead root cause analysis on systemic failures, translating QA findings into product, process, and policy recommendations that go beyond agent-level coaching.
  • Formalize Audit the Auditor as an ongoing control: define sample selection, alignment thresholds, root cause review, and evaluator-level remediation processes.
  • Ensure every evaluation closes with a documented coaching action; build the tracking mechanisms to measure whether coaching is translating into performance improvement over time.

Insights, Reporting & Stakeholder Partnership

  • Establish automated KPI reporting across all Volume Tier sites, tiers, and languages, eliminating manual processes.
  • Unify NPS detractor analysis across GE and ROW, ensuring global patterns surface in real time.
  • Build a Partner QA Performance Scorecard, establishing clear accountability for Calibration Accuracy, Evaluation Completeness, Critical Error Detection, Coaching Effectiveness.

AI & Technology Enablement

  • Lead the deployment of AutoQA (via Observe.AI) across Volume Tiers; partner with the Platform team to ensure appropriate sequencing.
  • Build and govern a clear accountability framework for AI-assisted quality tools and processes.

People & Culture Leadership

  • Lead a globally distributed team of Partner Quality Leads and Quality Insights Analysts.
  • Foster a One-Quality-Team culture that eliminates the cross-team divides: shared best practices, cross-regional learning, and proactive knowledge sharing.
  • Set high expectations and hold the team accountable for output quality, insight delivery, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Partner closely with peers to ensure one consistent quality voice across the portfolio.

Your Expertise:

  • 12+ years of experience in Customer/Community Support, Quality Assurance, or Contact Center Operations, with direct accountability for large-scale, multilingual QA programs.
  • 5+ years managing globally distributed QA teams across multiple languages, regions, and partner organizations in a 24/7 support environment.
  • Bachelor's Degree or equivalent experience, preferably in related field; MBA or Masters preferred
  • Experience with QA tooling platforms, including hands-on ownership of form design, calibration management, and AutoQA deployment.
  • Deep expertise in quality methodologies (COPC, AQS, Six Sigma, Lean), with a proven ability to apply them to high-volume, complex support environments.
  • Demonstrated track record of leading quality transformation, consolidating fragmented programs, driving measurable improvement in NPS/CSAT, and QA calibrations.
  • Experience deploying or scaling AI/ML assisted QA tools (AutoQA, predictive NPS/CSAT).
  • Strong executive presence: able to influence senior stakeholders, present a unified quality narrative in leadership forums, and drive alignment across stakeholders.
  • Experience managing vendor partner governance: calibration oversight, performance improvement plans, and escalation frameworks.

Preferred

  • COPC certification; Six Sigma Green or Black Belt.
  • Experience with Observe.AI.
  • Background in program management, change management, or organizational design within a high-growth tech environment.
  • Experience working in or closely with BPO/vendor governance models at scale (1,000+ partner FTEs across multiple sites and geographies).

Your Location:

This position is Canada - Remote Eligible. The role may include occasional work at an Airbnb office or attendance at offsites, as agreed to with your manager. While the position is Remote Eligible, you must live in a province where Airbnb Canada, Inc. has a registered entity. Currently we can hire in the following provinces: Ontario, British Columbia, Quebec, Alberta, and Saskatchewan. This list is continuously evolving, so please check back with your recruiter on what provinces you are eligible to work from.

Our Commitment To Inclusion & Belonging:

Airbnb is committed to working with the broadest talent pool possible. We believe diverse ideas foster innovation and engagement, and allow us to attract creatively-led people, and to develop the best products, services and solutions. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply.

We strive to also provide a disability inclusive application and interview process. If you are a candidate with a disability and require reasonable accommodation in order to submit an application, please contact us at: reasonableaccommodations@airbnb.com. Please include your full name, the role you’re applying for and the accommodation necessary to assist you with the recruiting process.

We ask that you only reach out to us if you are a candidate whose disability prevents you from being able to complete our online application.

We use automated tools to help our recruiting team efficiently screen a large volume of applications. All final hiring decisions are made by a human reviewer.

jobs.title: New Law Business Model: Solutions Engineer - Customer Success
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Boulder, CO
URL: https://newlawbusinessmodel.com

For over 10 years, New Law Business Model (NLBM) has been on a mission to liberate lawyers from outdated, soul-crushing practice models. We provide the heart-centered framework—Life & Legacy Planning®—and the high-octane membership products required to build thriving, relational firms. With a community of 800+ Personal Family Lawyer® firms nationwide, we leverage elite AI and automation to amplify humanity, delivering the practical education, tools, and "done-for-you" systems lawyers need to reclaim their time and build a lasting legacy. We obsess over real-world outcomes, not just vibes, to ensure our members move from survival mode to true flourishing.

The Mission

This Solutions Engineer role independently troubleshoots, maintains, and improves the technology and systems that power Accelerator. You’ll investigate complex technical problems, determine root causes, test and implement solutions, document the work, explain technical concepts clearly, and help create repeatable solutions that reduce recurring issues over time.

 

You are a systems navigator, technical troubleshooter, educator, and client advocate who gets the details right while meeting overwhelmed users with patience and clarity.

 

This role requires ownership, curiosity, patience, and a genuine desire to help people succeed—not simply close tickets.

Job requirements

What You’ll Do

Pillar 1: Member Support, Troubleshooting & Education

  • Own complex technical troubleshooting from discovery through resolution, including root-cause analysis, testing, implementation, documentation, and follow-through.

  • Meet members where they are technically, turning complex issues into clear, approachable guidance through Loom, email, phone, or whatever channel works best.

  • Help members understand not just what to do, but why it matters, so they feel confident handling similar situations in the future; coordinate with external partners and maintain full accountability through resolution. 

Pillar 2: Accelerator Platform & Systems Operations

  • Administer and support the Accelerator technology environment across GoHighLevel, HubSpot, Asana, and connected systems, including the relationships between HubSpot firms, orders, contracts, Asana implementation projects, and Accelerator member accounts.

  • Complete approved account builds, updates, pauses, reactivations, migrations, and technical closeout tasks while troubleshooting workflows, pipelines, calendars, forms, permissions, and settings.

  • Investigate deliverability, phone/SMS, domains, DNS, integrations, and data issues; maintain accurate records and provide bounded support for related legacy platforms as assigned.

Pillar 3: Quality Assurance, Integrations & AI-Assisted Work

  • Use AI thoughtfully and approved integration tools to investigate issues, interpret errors, and complete member requests.

  • Verify recommendations and changes against actual system settings, reliable documentation, and realistic test scenarios.

  • Investigate APIs, webhooks, authentication, logs, and field mappings; coordinate complex development needs, document results and limitations, and protect confidential member information.

Pillar 4: Documentation, Knowledge Sharing & Improvement

  • Learn, document, and progressively take ownership of recurring technical processes.

  • Document technical knowledge so teammates can work confidently and apply repeatable solutions.

  • Identify patterns across recurring technical issues and recommend repeatable fixes, documentation, automation, or product improvements.

     

What Success Looks Like

  • Members receive accurate solutions, timely updates, clear next steps, and greater confidence using the technology that supports their firms.

  • Technical requests are handled with strong ownership and reliable follow-through, while changes are tested, reviewed, documented, and implemented thoughtfully.

  • Recurring issues lead to better instructions, reusable solutions, or system improvements that teammates can access and apply confidently; you identify problems early and help move members from frustration to forward momentum.

     

Who You Are

  • You have hands-on experience administering and troubleshooting GoHighLevel and HubSpot across multiple accounts, including workflows, order forms, contracts, client records, and support tickets.

  • You understand workflows, pipelines, snapshots, calendars, forms, permissions, account configuration, and the dependencies between shared systems and firm-specific customizations.

  • You are a patient, compassionate teacher who explains technical concepts in plain language and can guide clients through solutions over Loom or Zoom.

  • You understand APIs, webhooks, authentication, JSON, logs, data mapping, email, phone/SMS, DNS, and calendar integrations; you use AI responsibly, document as you go, share knowledge, and own follow-through.

Helpful additional experience includes law-firm or professional-services operations, estate planning, Keap, Lawmatics, Make, Zapier, n8n, data migrations, reconciliation, or light JavaScript, TypeScript, or Python.

 

Compensation & Benefits

  • Position Type: Full-Time, Non-Exempt (W2) 40 Hours / Week

  • Hourly Base Wage: Pay Rate: $40.87–$45.67 ($85,000 – $95,000 / annualized)

    • Starting base pay is determined by factors including geographic location, applicable experience, skills, and internal equity. Non-exempt employees are eligible for overtime pay in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

  • Work Schedule & Compliance: Requires minimum (4) hours core schedule to overlap with Pacific Time (e.g., 9:00 AM – 1:00 PM PT)

Why Join NLBM? 

  • 100% Remote Work at a Profitable, Growing Company

  • Recession-Proof Industry, Product, and Audience

  • Comprehensive Benefits Package (Health, Dental, Vision)

  • 401K Retirement Program

  • Flexible Paid Time Off

  • Opportunities for Career Growth and Leadership Development

  • Be Part of a Mission-Driven Company Transforming the Legal Industry

 

At NLBM, you’ll have the opportunity to make a lasting impact, scale your career in leadership, and be part of a passionate, supportive team driving innovation and change.

 

This role operates under a Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) model. Employees are expected to provide their own computer and internet connection, meeting minimum requirements (including at least 16GB RAM) to perform work duties. The company provides required software and system access, and reimburses reasonable and necessary business expenses including a monthly internet/technology allowance as required by law.

 

New Law Business Model (NLBM) respects your time and work. Any portfolio materials, technical breakdowns, or operational insights submitted during this application process are requested solely for the purpose of assessing your qualifications for this position. NLBM will not use, publish, or commercially exploit any material submitted during your application process without your express written consent. jobs.title: Mercury: Creative Director - Brand Narrative
jobs.description:
Headquarters: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States

In 1977, Charles and Ray Eames began a film with a picnic beside Chicago’s lakefront. Over the next nine minutes, Powers of Ten traveled out toward distant galaxies and back into the microscopic world inside a human hand. An enormous subject became a journey you could follow, built around a simple change in perspective. Images, language, movement, and sound brought the idea to life together. 

That’s the kind of creative thinking we’re looking for at Mercury: finding a compelling idea inside something complex, then bringing together the people and crafts that make it unforgettable.

We’re looking for a Creative Director to build and lead Brand Narrative, a new team within Brand Creative. You’ll turn company strategy, product truths, customer insight, and cultural observations into original concepts for our most important launches, campaigns, and brand moments. You’ll originate ideas yourself and stay closely involved as they become finished work.

Your background might be in art direction, design, or copywriting. What matters is your ability to develop exceptional concepts, recognize the best idea wherever it comes from, and bring the whole creative studio together to make it real. Whatever your starting discipline, you’ll bring deep experience in film-led storytelling.

You’ll lead Brand Narrative in close creative partnership with your peers leading Brand Design and Writing. Together, you’ll shape concepts, language, and visual expression from the beginning, bringing distinct perspectives and shared ownership to the work. You’ll contribute strong ideas of your own, invite others to challenge and improve them, and build on theirs. This is a role for someone who enjoys making work together, not developing ideas in isolation and handing them off.

You’ll also shape what Brand Narrative becomes. That means building its culture, developing its people, and establishing ways of working that make the entire studio more creatively ambitious. The opportunity is to make great work while building a team that can keep making it.

What you’ll do

In your first year, your focus will be roughly 70% leading creative development for our highest-priority launches and campaigns, and 30% building the Brand Narrative function.

  • Originate and lead big creative ideas. Partner with Product Marketing and Brand Marketing on the brief, then turn the agreed audience, opportunity, and product proof into original creative concepts. Develop ideas that can take distinctive forms across film, social, out-of-home, digital, experiences, and partnerships.
  • Bring ambitious concepts to life with your creative peers and the full studio. Work side by side with the Brand Design and Writing leads and their teams from the earliest explorations through delivery. Develop ideas together, exchange thoughtful critique, and make creative choices that draw on each discipline’s expertise. Stay hands-on, contribute through your own craft, and partner closely with Motion and Production throughout. For film, remain closely involved through scripts, visual development, production, and the final edit.
  • Build audience and distribution thinking into the idea. Shape concepts around how people will discover, watch, and share the work. Work with marketing partners to consider channels and viewing contexts from the beginning, so the work belongs where people encounter it rather than simply being resized to fit.
  • Push beyond the first good answer, and learn quickly. Lead thoughtful concept development and critique. Use rough scripts, prototypes, and AI tools to test ideas quickly, learn, and move the strongest work forward. Know when to keep exploring and when to commit, then protect what makes an idea interesting through feedback and production.
  • Find opportunities before a brief arrives. Bring curiosity about Mercury’s products, customers, and the wider world. Develop proactive ideas and cultural opportunities that give the brand something meaningful to say or do.
  • Help decide where creative ambition matters most. Partner early with Product Marketing, Brand Marketing, Product Design, Comms, and Insights. Help identify which moments deserve our largest creative investment, present recommendations to senior leadership, and use results from marketing and insights partners to inform what comes next.
  • Build and lead Brand Narrative. Define the team’s purpose, priorities, creative standards, and ways of working. Help hire and develop the team, shaping its structure and capabilities. Set clear expectations, and coach people to grow their judgment and conceptual strength.
  • Create a culture where the best idea wins. Make room for experimentation, honest feedback, and contributions across disciplines. Lead with generosity and conviction, share ownership of the work, and help people challenge one another without making creativity a competition for credit.
  • Build practices that strengthen the work. Establish a clear path from insight and an agreed brief to concept and execution, with useful critique and close collaboration throughout. Develop relationships with external creatives and agencies who can add a distinctive perspective or capability when needed.

What you’ll bring

  • A strong creative foundation in art direction, design, or copywriting. Your portfolio shows original concepts developed into ambitious, well-crafted work across multiple formats. You can explain what you contributed, how the idea evolved, and how collaboration made it better.
  • Deep film experience. You’ve developed film-led ideas from concept through production, with strong instincts for story, scripts, performance, pacing, and sound. You understand how these choices work together to make an audience feel something, not just make a film look good.
  • A track record of deep creative collaboration with design and writing peers. You’ve led ambitious multidisciplinary work from concept through production by building trusted partnerships. You bring a clear point of view, listen closely, work through creative disagreements constructively, and recognize when someone else’s approach makes the work stronger. You can show how your collaborators shaped the outcome, not just what you personally originated.
  • Strong taste, cultural awareness, and product curiosity. You can get close to a complex business or product, find the human truth within it, and turn that understanding into something clear, surprising, and memorable.
  • Experience developing creative people and shaping how a team works. You give specific, useful feedback, set a high bar with care, and create an environment where people can take creative risks. You’re excited to build a new function, including the everyday practices that give it a culture.
  • Clear communication and sound judgment. You can rally people around an ambitious concept, explain why it deserves investment, and navigate competing perspectives without losing the idea. You take ownership in ambiguous situations and balance creative ambition with the need to move work forward.

What success looks like

A year in, you’ll have led major launches and film-led campaigns from original concept through finished work, with Brand Design and Writing as creative partners from the beginning. The studio’s disciplines will have shaped the work together, with audience and distribution informing the creative approach.

Brand Narrative will have a clear identity, shared creative standards, and working practices that help people test and develop stronger ideas together. Alongside planned launches, you’ll have established a pipeline of proactive opportunities that gives Mercury more ways to express its product ambition with originality and cultural relevance.

Please include a portfolio featuring film-led work and broader campaign concepts. We’d love to understand your role in developing the ideas, the choices you made through production, and how you brought the work to life with others.

jobs.title: Netlify: Senior Staff Data Scientist
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote

About the Team:

Netlify’s Data team helps the company understand and improve the full product-led growth journey, from activation and engagement through conversion, retention, and monetization. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, and Growth to uncover opportunities, evaluate investments, and understand what drives customer and business outcomes.

We’re hiring a Senior Staff Data Scientist to deepen how data shapes our product and growth strategy. You’ll develop an end-to-end understanding of the PLG journey, proactively identify opportunities, and turn complex data into hypotheses, experiments, and recommendations that influence where we invest and what we build. This is a highly autonomous role for someone who can move from identifying an important question to shaping the approach, defining success, and driving toward an answer.

What You'll Do:

  • Own the analytical understanding of Netlify’s PLG performance across activation, engagement, conversion, monetization, and retention, identifying opportunities before they become requests
  • Partner with Product and Engineering leadership to turn behavioral insights into product bets, defining what to test, how to measure it, and what the results mean
  • Lead experimentation from hypothesis through decision, including study design, methodology, success metrics, guardrails, analysis, and recommendations
  • Apply statistical rigor where it matters while recognizing when there is enough signal to make a decision and move forward, and help teams develop that same judgment
  • Build scalable analytical systems like semantic models, trusted metrics, proactive monitoring, and AI-powered agents  that surface opportunities without waiting to be asked
  • Use AI to investigate faster, automate recurring analytical work, and test more hypotheses without sacrificing the judgment that makes the output useful
  • Identify gaps in measurement, event instrumentation, and metric definitions, and partner with Data and Product Engineering to close them
  • Serve as a trusted analytical partner to PLG leadership, using evidence and product judgment to influence investment decisions and roadmap priorities
  • Influence product strategy through evidence, product instincts, and a clear point of view, without relying on formal authority to do it

What You'll Bring:

  • 8+ years of experience in product analytics, growth analytics, or data science, with a track record of high ownership and measurable impact on PLG or consumer product outcomes
  • Deep understanding of product and growth dynamics across activation, engagement, conversion, monetization, and retention
  • Demonstrated ability to turn behavioral data into product hypotheses and carry them from insight through experimentation and measured outcomes
  • Deep experimentation expertise: study design, statistical reasoning, causal inference, and the judgment to know when an experiment has told you what you need to know
  • Experience building analytical systems such as metrics layers, monitoring frameworks, or semantic models that teams can rely on over time
  • An AI-native approach to analysis: you use AI tools actively to accelerate investigation, automate repetitive work, and surface patterns faster
  • A track record of influencing senior stakeholders and product direction through analytical reasoning, clear recommendations, and sound judgment
  • Comfort operating with significant autonomy in ambiguous problem spaces, including determining which questions are most important to answer
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in distributed environments, with the ability to make complex findings clear and recommendations actionable

This Role is a Great Fit If:

  • You're energized by finding the opportunity before anyone thought to ask - proactive discovery is how you naturally work, not a mode you shift into
  • You think like a product person who happens to be exceptionally rigorous with data, not a data person who occasionally weighs in on product
  •  You thrive when the problem isn't handed to you - you'd rather define the question worth asking than answer the one that landed in your queue
  • You get excited about building systems that keep working after you've moved on to the next problem
  • You're comfortable making a call with imperfect information and can articulate clearly why you made it
  • You enjoy being a thought partner to senior leaders - shaping how they think about investment and opportunity, not just supporting decisions already made
  • You work well in a remote-first, async environment where written clarity and self-direction matter more than proximity
  • You're drawn to roles where the measure of success is outcomes, decisions made, bets tested, metrics moved, not volume of output produced

Applying

Not sure you meet 100% of our qualifications? Please apply anyway!

When applying please include: 

A resume or short listing of your job history & skills (link to a LinkedIn profile would be fine). We appreciate a cover letter explaining why you would enjoy working in this role at Netlify to get to know you a bit better, though this is not required and will not impact your application. Our mission is to “build a better web” and that cannot be done without a diversity of skill sets, backgrounds and thoughts. 

Of everything we've ever built at Netlify, we are most proud of our team. Netlify is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are devoted to building a team of people with diverse backgrounds and lifestyles. Driving equality empowers our team, enables us to innovate, and helps us maintain a more inclusive environment. We don’t discriminate against employees or applicants based on gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, age, race, military/veteran status, citizenship, pregnancy status, or any other differences. If we can do anything to provide a better interview, i.e. accommodate a disability, then please let us know by emailing accommodations@netlify.com. 

 

About Netlify

Netlify is the most popular way to build, deploy, and scale modern web applications, empowering everyone from fast moving solo developers to enterprise teams. Millions of developers and organizations rely on Netlify as their platform of choice for composing web applications that are production ready, performant, and flexible. Now, as we embrace the next era of software development, we are embedding the same fluid, intuitive experience into the Agent Experience (AX), making it just as simple for intelligent agents to understand, interact with, and act on our platform as it is for developers. Whether your user is human or machine, Netlify ensures the path from idea to URL is seamless, fast, and deeply reliable.

We are a Series D company that has raised over $200M from investors such as Andreessen Horowitz, Kleiner Perkins, EQT, Bessemer, BOND, and Menlo Ventures. As a fully distributed company, we aim to create a company culture where the best idea can come from anywhere and strive to be thoughtful, compassionate, and collaborative in our work. If this sounds like something you’d like to be part of, we’re excited to connect with you!

At Netlify, we are committed to a compensation philosophy that prioritizes fairness and equity, positions our employee compensation competitively in the market, recognizes and rewards performance, and takes a comprehensive approach to our rewards package. jobs.title: Mercury: Business Continuity Management Lead
jobs.description:
Headquarters: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States

About the Role

Mercury is seeking a Business Continuity Management (BCM) Lead to build and lead an enterprise-wide continuity program as we prepare to become a bank. As part of the Risk team, this leader will establish practical standards, clear accountability, and tested capabilities to maintain critical services and recover effectively from disruptions, with direct visibility to the CRO and senior leadership.

This role fills the need for a dedicated leader to coordinate BCM across the organization. The ideal candidate combines deep continuity and resilience expertise with the judgment to build a proportionate program in a fast-moving environment, working effectively with Engineering, Operations, Product, Information Security, Legal, Compliance, and business teams.

The BCM Lead will own the enterprise framework, coordination, oversight, and reporting. Business and technology owners will remain accountable for their continuity plans and recovery execution.Because this is a new program, the Lead will be hands-on in the initial build: facilitating the first round of BIAs and plans side by side with owners, running exercises, and driving identified gaps through remediation. This leader will also work closely with Engineering on technology disaster recovery and with relevant teams on incident response, crisis management, and third-party resilience.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and implement Mercury’s enterprise BCM framework, policies, standards, governance, and operating model, with a prioritized implementation roadmap aligned to bank-launch readiness and critical services.
  • Partner with business owners to identify critical services, conduct business impact analyses (customer, financial, operational, and regulatory), and map dependencies across people, processes, technology, facilities, and third parties, including single points of failure.
  • Establish recovery time objectives (RTOs) and recovery point objectives (RPOs), where applicable, with business and technology owners; challenge gaps between objectives and recovery capabilities.
  • Set standards for continuity plans and recovery procedures, and facilitate and support accountable owners in developing actionable plans and alternative operating arrangements.
  • Coordinate business continuity with technology disaster recovery, incident response, and crisis management, with clear activation criteria, escalation paths, and communications responsibilities.
  • Design and lead a risk-based exercise program, from tabletop simulations to end-to-end recovery tests, and drive lessons learned, remediation tracking, and verification that gaps are closed.
  • Partner with Third-Party Risk Management and vendor owners to assess critical provider recovery capabilities, contingency arrangements, and concentration dependencies.
  • Embed continuity considerations into new products, material business changes, and technology implementations.
  • Establish metrics and reporting that give management and relevant committees visibility into readiness, testing outcomes, material gaps, and overdue remediation.
  • Build and lead a growing BCM team, including hiring and developing analysts as the program scales over the next year.
  • Deliver role-based training and promote awareness of continuity responsibilities across the organization.
  • Support regulatory examinations and bank-launch readiness reviews with accurate documentation and evidence of recovery capability.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in business continuity management, operational resilience, disaster recovery, or a related discipline within a fintech, financial institution, technology company, or other highly regulated environment.
  • Demonstrated experience building or materially enhancing an enterprise BCM program, including governance, implementation, testing, and reporting.
  • Strong skills in business impact analysis, critical-service identification, dependency mapping, and recovery objective development.
  • Experience developing actionable continuity plans and leading exercises that test recovery assumptions and expose gaps.
  • Sufficient technical fluency to work with Engineering on cloud services, system dependencies, data recovery, and technology disaster recovery.
  • Working knowledge of third-party risk management, including assessing critical vendor recovery capabilities, contingency arrangements and concentration risk.
  • Proven ability to drive cross-functional remediation through influence, with a clear view of where BCM oversight ends and business or technology ownership begins.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain readiness gaps and tradeoffs to senior leadership.
  • Experience managing a team of Business Continuity analysts.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Familiarity with banking supervisory expectations for business continuity, and operational resilience.
  • Experience operating in a company-building or bank-building environment.
  • Familiarity with recognized continuity standards, such as ISO 22301, and BCM tools for plan management, exercises, and issue tracking.
  • Relevant professional certification, such as CBCP or MBCI.

Leadership Attributes

  • Pragmatic, first-principles builder who turns ambiguous needs into clear priorities and designs a program that fits Mercury’s operations and scale.
  • Takes ownership and follows through from identified gaps to demonstrated recovery.
  • Collaborative, low-ego, and effective across the three lines of defense.
  • Calm under pressure and able to facilitate clear decisions during disruptions.
  • Able to challenge constructively, distinguish material gaps from theoretical concerns, and avoid over-engineering.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

Mercury values diversity & belonging and is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. All individuals seeking employment at Mercury are considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic.
